chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“If you do not know whether you have prayed four or five, then perform the two sajdahs of sahw after your taslim, then give salām after them.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: As for the two sajdahs of sahw after the taslim, the person says in his سجود. We have already explained earlier that the place of the two sajdahs of sahw is after the taslim, and this is also further confirmed by what he narrated:

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rak'ahs in the prayer being doubted
key_terms.تَسْلِيمِكَ: your taslim, the concluding salām of the prayer
key_terms.خَمْسًا: five rak'ahs in the prayer being doubted
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations prescribed for inadvertence or doubt in salat
key_terms.سُجُودِهِ: his prostration, referring to what is said during the prostration
key_terms.مَوْضِعُهُمَا: their proper place or position in the sequence of the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he prayed four or five rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts whether he prayed four or five rak'ahs: he should perform the two sajdahs of sahw after the taslim, then give salām afterward. The accompanying statement of al-Shaykh affirms that the prescribed place of sajdatay al-sahw is after the taslim.
